answer: A bookbinder guild record with binding commission chain works as the gate: commissions bound for one bindery over years. Each of 447 aliases needs its own commission chains, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. Call it the spiral rule: fakes pay per head, the honest pay once, the nebula record is open for audit, and the wander window is too short for 447 aliases to earn their price back.
